subject: Follow-up: Procurement constraints (prepay / no PO) — next steps
content:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Lindsay Cheng <lindsay.cheng@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro + procurement

Hi Lindsay / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the procurement constraints you mentioned:

- Procurement position: Acme Health currently does not accept vendor POs for SaaS spend above $50k unless there is an approved enterprise contract. You mentioned the preferred path is prepay on a corporate card or via marketplace where possible.
- Risk: Your security/compliance team requires SOC2 evidence and a standard DPIA before any private deployment starts (we already shared SOC2 report on the call).
- Immediate ask from your side: Can Redwood accept a prepay-only arrangement for the first 6 months while you complete internal legal review? If not, you asked whether we can escalate an exception for a no-PO policy.

Proposed next steps:
1) I will loop in our commercial ops to review the no-PO exception path and confirm what approvals are required.
2) If prepay works, we can onboard through our marketplace (reduces procurement friction) — I will check marketplace availability in your cloud region.
3) I'll attach a short exception request form we can complete together to speed the finance review.

Attachments: Acme_PO_Policy.pdf (your internal policy copy you shared on the call) — thanks for sending; redwood_exception_form.xlsx (draft exception request for finance/legal).

If either of you can confirm whether prepay on corporate card is possible for the pilot, that will get us moving faster. Otherwise I’ll request an approval path and timeline from our ops team.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0137

--

On Tue, 3 Nov 2026 at 16:27, Lindsay Cheng <lindsay.cheng@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> From: Lindsay Cheng <lindsay.cheng@acmehealth.com>
> To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
> Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmehealth.com>
> Date: 2026-11-03T16:27:00-08:00
> Subject: Re: Intro + procurement
>
> Hi Vanessa — thanks for the recap. Correct on the PO policy. A couple clarifications:
>
> - We can do prepay on card for pilots up to $20k, but anything expected >$20k in 6 months will require an enterprise contract and purchase order.
> - Marketplace purchases are preferred (reduces our internal approvals), but our platform team must confirm available SKUs for the commitment levels we discussed.
> - We cannot sign any deviation from our standard PO flow without legal sign-off — historically that takes 3–4 weeks.
>
> I’ve attached the PO policy for reference (Acme_PO_Policy.pdf). If Redwood can accept a prepay up to $20k that would be ideal for the pilot. If not, we’ll need an exception and I’ll need to send the internal request to our procurement governance board.
>
> Lindsay
> Procurement Director | Acme Health
> lindsay.cheng@acmehealth.com | +1 (212) 555-0199
>

On Wed, 4 Nov 2026 at 09:14, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
> To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
> Cc: Lindsay Cheng <lindsay.cheng@acmehealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmehealth.com>
> Date: 2026-11-04T09:14:00-08:00
> Subject: Fwd: Intro + procurement — request for exception / guidance>
>
> Team — fwding a short thread with Acme. They can prepay up to $20k for a pilot but cannot accept PO without a 3–4 week legal approval. They asked whether we can: (A) accept prepay for the pilot (fine); or (B) escalate an exception for no-PO path for the initial term if we expect spend >$20k.
>
> Questions for ops/legal:
> - Is there a standard exception we can offer (short-term prepay with credit memos / refund policy) when customers cannot issue POs?
> - For marketplace route: do we have an offering SKU that maps to a 6-month pilot and supports card/prepay billing?
> - If we escalate a no-PO exception, what approvals are required (finance + legal + CRO signoff?) and typical SLA to get a decision?
>
> I’ve attached the redwood_exception_form.xlsx — can one of you take point and advise next steps / required fields we should fill before sending to Acme?
>
> Thanks,
> Vanessa
>
> --

On Thu, 5 Nov 2026 at 09:41, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
> To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
> Cc: Lindsay Cheng <lindsay.cheng@acmehealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmehealth.com>
> Date: 2026-11-05T09:41:00-08:00
> Subject: Re: Fwd: Intro + procurement — request for exception / guidance>
>
> Vanessa — thanks for the thread. Quick internal note:
>
> - We have a documented short-term exception pattern: run pilot on prepay (card or marketplace) up to $25k with an internal exception form + finance acknowledgement. For anything above $25k we require CFO-level approval and a legal deviation memo (typical 2–3 week turnaround).
> - Marketplace is preferable where available — it reduces billing complexity and we can often offer 30-day refund terms for pilots. I can confirm SKU availability by EOD using the marketplace team.
> - Action: Marissa, can you prepare the exception package (fill the attached redwood_exception_form.xlsx with the buyer details and expected spend; include the Acme_PO_Policy.pdf as context) and route to finance for acknowledgement? I’ll review and prepare a short approval memo if we need CRO/CFO signoff.
>
> Vanessa — please ask Acme if they can increase prepay to $25k for Redwood to avoid escalation. If not, we’ll proceed with the exception package.
>
> Karthik Iyer
> Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
> karthik_iyer@redwood.com

>
> Attachments referenced: redwood_exception_form.xlsx (draft), Acme_PO_Policy.pdf (customer-supplied)
